newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela offers tax break for heavy crude schemes.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela offers tax break for heavy crude schemes.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has decided to reduce royalty taxes levied on projects to develop the country's massive extra-heavy crude reserves, Energy and Mines vice Minister Evanan Romero said Tuesday.
Under the tax break scheme, "we will adjust the royalty according to the profitability of each project," Romero told reporters.
The new tax scale could see the standard 16.67 percent royalty tax on all oil projects reduced to as little as 1.5 percent, he said.
The aim was "to give the investor a break and help him to recover his investment," Romero said.

Romero added that projects to develop the resources of Venezuela's Orinoco Tar Belt would be subject to a 34 percent corporate income tax rate, not the 67 percent rate normally levied on oil projects.
Petroleos de Venezuela subsidiaries have signed joint venture agreements with several foreign companies to upgrade and market synthetic crudes from the Orinoco Tar Belt.
On Tuesday, PDVSA unit Lagoven signed a $2.3 billion deal with Mobil Oil Corp to produce about 100,000 bpd of synthetic crude from the Cerro Negro area of the tar belt.
